pr.title: Skip a host that is installed but does not run instead of retrying its clone
pr.head: cd632c84a8748f73dec3d3771a2c0a03f42049dd

summary: The installer adds Projector to Claude Code and Codex through each host’s plugin manager. Finding a command on PATH does not prove that command can run: a package can remain installed after its native executable disappears.

The installer now probes --version before host operations. A broken host is skipped during all, rejected with exit 69 during a host-only install, and reported as host-broken during status. The other host and the optional gh stack extension can still install.

cards.title: Review evidence
cards.html: This fork head was reviewed by reading; its installer and tests did not run locally. The exact-head check workflow awaits maintainer approval, so CI supplied no test evidence. No findings or suggestions were identified.

groups.title: Stop before a broken host’s plugin commands
groups.kicker: Probe host startup and give each install mode its own result
intro: The shared host_runs helper invokes the selected executable with --version and discards its output. A failed probe produces a reinstall message instead of being mistaken for a slow marketplace clone or a missing plugin.

all continues past a broken host and counts only usable hosts toward success. A targeted host install exits 69 before creating its configuration directory or removing legacy links. Status reporting emits one broken-host warning and suppresses a misleading missing-hooks row.

files.note: Adds the startup probe and routes failure through targeted installs, all, and status.

checks.text: Reading both install functions confirms the probe precedes directory creation, legacy-link removal, and marketplace commands.
Traced both all branches: a failed probe skips only that host, then reaches the other host and gh-stack installation before deciding exit 69.

files.note: Documents skipped and host-broken rows and the unavailable-host exit behavior.

groups.title: Exercise unavailable hosts through the installer
groups.kicker: Keep the real installer while replacing external host commands
intro: The fixture replaces a fake host executable with one that fails every invocation. Each case then calls the real installer interface and checks its exit status, warning, or recorded commands.

The cases cover broken Codex and Claude Code during all, host-only refusal, no usable host, and diagnostic status. They also check that broken hosts receive no marketplace command or retry and that unaffected components continue.

checks.text: These tests were inspected, not executed locally. CI for this fork has not run because the workflow needs maintainer approval.

files.note: Adds a failing-host fixture and five installer behavior regressions.
